Leju and Zhaofeng disclose results from 15 factory humanoids

The companies report about 98% loading success, around 1,000 operating hours and over 60,000 parts, while cycle time still trails workers.

Pandaily ↗16 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Results from an operating line

Leju and Zhaofeng presented their joint loading solution in Hangzhou on October 15. They say 15 humanoids have worked routinely at 15 stations for over two months, handling more than ten part types and accumulating about 1,000 hours and over 60,000 parts.

Success rate versus speed

Reported loading success is about 98%, but robot cycles take roughly 35 to under 40 seconds versus about 15 seconds for a skilled worker. These figures come from reporting and company disclosures, not a comprehensive independent comparison.

Flexibility is the application

The robots address varied products and small batches between existing automated processes. Leju says it divides loading into over 30 reusable modules. Transfer to another factory still requires adaptation to parts, equipment interfaces and safety requirements.
